skill: Infer the sign of a monomial slope function in each open quadrant and select every true universal sign statement.
reasoning_steps: Read y'=f(x,y), identify axes as zero sets.
Determine the sign using coefficient sign and parity of x and y powers (or one test point per open quadrant).
Compare each offered positive/negative claim to the sign in its quadrant; select true claims and None of the above only if all substantive claims fail.
response_contract: Checkbox fields, each with complete true/false choice bank. Usually three distinct quadrant claims, optionally None of the above. Canonical example is prose statements with a subset conclusion.
difficulty: Moderate captured questions use nonzero cxy; hard and one undifferentiated supplemental question introduce squared factors. Parity extensions are source-supported at their corresponding level.
invariants: Open quadrants avoid axes; nonzero monomials have constant nonzero sign in each quadrant.
Slope sign is f sign; no differential equation solving or integration required.
Prompt, claims, field keys, sign diagram, answer and explanation must agree.
Complete checkbox bank and solution progression must replay original parameters.
permitted_variations: Nonzero coefficient magnitude and sign. Magnitude is irrelevant to sign; sign reverses all quadrant signs.
Which three quadrants appear, their order, and positive/negative assertion in each are incidental assignments and can vary independently.
Truth subset including zero, one, two or three substantive truths; optional None must track empty subset.
Source-supported exponent parity where difficulty permits, with derived signs and diagrams.

fixed_features.feature: Axes bounding four standard open quadrants
fixed_features.justification: Target KP and all observed monomial zero sets; shifted rectangular regions belong to adjacent KP 17592186172041.
Consistent observed workload; no need to increase count.

source_refs: tutorial 790a4898-1668-5214-a911-83977b559c34: We then calculate the slope at each point and record each answer in the table.
prerequisite 51d10b95-2ba8-5125-8f0d-b21455269c1e: To determine the sign of f(x,y) in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

source_observations.canonical: -2xy; II negative false, III negative true, IV positive true. Diagram inspected: I/III minus and II/IV plus.
source_observations.moderate: 2xy claims I+/II+/III+ gives T/F/T; 6xy II-/III+/IV- gives T/T/T; -5xy I+/II-/IV+ gives F/F/T; -xy I+/II+/IV- gives F/T/F; 9xy I-/II-/IV+ gives F/T/F. Positive diagram inspected: I/III plus, II/IV minus.
source_observations.other: xy^2 supplemental: I-/II-/III- gives F/T/T; 8x^2y^2 hard: I-/III+/IV- gives F/T/F; -4xy^2 hard: I-/II+/IV- all true.

gaps: Canonical example lacks its answer-field bank in the canonical-example object, but all eight supplied question objects provide full banks. Supplemental xy^2 has terse prose solution and no declared difficulty.
essential_vs_incidental: The sign/parity operation and open quadrants are essential. Coefficient sign, qualifying quadrant labels, claim polarity, choice order and truth count are answer-bearing assignments, not fixed pedagogical requirements.
